### Summary

After reconstruction each face has two states, one from each side, and the solver turns them into the one flux
the face carries. snapy has six solvers behind one interface; the deck picks one for all three directions. The
solver also returns the face pressure the $x_1$ pressure force and the well-balanced path need, and three of the
six cannot. The shipped decks name `lmars` (7), `hllc` (6) or `shallow-roe` (9).

<!-- generated reader-reference: riemann -->
For hydrodynamics, omitting the `riemann-solver` block preserves `hllc` ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp:33`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp#L33)); a present block without `type` selects `roe` ([`src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp:27`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp#L27)). These are distinct parser paths at source pin `919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274`.
<!-- end reader-reference: riemann -->

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One flux per face from $\mathbf W^{\mathrm L}_f, \mathbf W^{\mathrm R}_f$, rows renamed by @eq-ch04-riemann-frame.

**Data.** Reads the two face states (and the equation of state); writes $\mathbf F_a$ and, on $x_1$, the face pressure.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, in `HydroImpl::forward`, once per direction after the reconstruction.

**Activation.** `dynamics/riemann-solver/{type,dir}`; the generated statement above distinguishes the two parser paths.

**Guarantee / limits.** Consistent solvers; only `lmars`, `hllc`, `roe` write a face pressure.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch04-riemann-tests; `test_riemann.release`, the probe run, `operator_check.py` `[C8]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf W^{\mathrm L}_f, \mathbf W^{\mathrm R}_f$ the left and right primitive
states of face $f$ (appendix A, notation group 4); $v_\perp$ the face-normal velocity and $v_{\parallel,1}, v_{\parallel,2}$ the two
tangential ones in the face-local frame [m s$^{-1}$]; $p_f$ the face pressure [Pa]; `dim` the code's direction
index, 3 for $x_1$, 2 for $x_2$, 1 for $x_3$.

### Derivation

#### Why one solver body serves all three directions

1. *The flux through a face depends on the normal velocity.* Mass, energy and every species move with
   $v_\perp$, the normal momentum also carries $p$[^rg-b356ccc3d610], and the tangential momenta move passively.
2. *The code renames rows instead of rotating vectors.* For direction `dim` the normal momentum row is

   $$
   \mathrm{ivx} = \mathrm{IPR} - \mathrm{dim},
   $$ {#eq-ch04-riemann-frame}

   and the tangential rows are the next two in cyclic order, `ivy = IVX + ((ivx - IVX) + 1) % 3` and
   `ivz = IVX + ((ivx - IVX) + 2) % 3`. With `IVX, IVY, IVZ, IPR` $= 1, 2, 3, 4$ this gives `ivx` $= 1, 2, 3$ for
   $x_1, x_2, x_3$.
3. *It is a permutation.* For each `dim` the three rows are distinct, so every momentum component is read and
   written once; `operator_check.py` `[C8]` lists them. A renaming involves no arithmetic, so it adds no
   round-off.
4. *On a curved grid the renaming is not enough.* The velocity components are covariant or panel components, not
   components in the face's orthonormal frame. `lmars`, `hllc` and `shallow-roe` call `prim2local{1,2,3}_` on
   both states before solving and `flux2global{1,2,3}_` on the flux after (@sec-ch04-gnomonic); `roe` does not. In the code, @eq-ch04-riemann-frame is `ivx` ({{< code src/riemann/lmars_impl.h lmars_impl >}}).

#### Why some solvers refuse a run

1. *The $x_1$ sweep always asks for a face pressure* when the block has more than one $x_1$ cell and the
   equation of state is not `shallow-water`: `HydroImpl::reset` allocates `_face_pressure1` whenever
   $n_{c1} > 1$, and `forward` passes it.
2. *`upwind`, `plume-roe` and `shallow-roe` refuse a face-pressure request* with "Face-pressure output is not
   implemented".
3. *Hence `upwind` and `plume-roe` cannot run a compressible deck with a resolved $x_1$ axis*; the probe run
   stops on the first stage with that message for both. `shallow-roe` runs because its equation of state turns
   the request off.

: The six solvers at the pin. "Shipped decks" counts `examples/*.yaml`. {#tbl-ch04-riemann-types}

**The scalar solver.** `ScalarImpl` requires `upwind` ("Passive scalars currently require the upwind solver")
and calls it with the hydro mass flux as the fourth argument, so the scalar's flux is the mass flux times the
upwind mixing ratio (@sec-ch08-scalar). Used as the hydro solver, the same argument would be the hydro's own
flux buffer.

### Code

**A minimal input.**

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dir`[^rg-a2031683b1d7].
```yaml
dynamics:
  riemann-solver:
    type: lmars    # one of roe, lmars, hllc, upwind, shallow-roe, plume-roe
    dir: omni      # read by shallow-roe only; it requires xy or yz
```

**What the parser accepts and refuses.** `RiemannSolverOptionsImpl::from_yaml` and the factory apply, in order:

1. *No `riemann-solver` block*: the options object is returned as constructed (see the generated defaults above)
   ({{< code src/riemann/riemann_solver.hpp RiemannSolverOptionsImpl >}}).
2. *A block takes only `type` and `dir`*; any other key is refused by `check_keys` ("unknown key
   'dynamics/riemann-solver/foo'. Valid keys: type, dir").
3. *Inside a block a missing key uses the parser fallback*; the type is stated above, and the direction is `omni`
   ({{< code src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp RiemannSolverOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}).
4. *An unknown type is refused* by `RiemannSolverImpl::create` ("RiemannSolver: unknown type exact").
5. *`shallow-roe` refuses `dir: omni`* when it runs, and on a gnomonic grid requires `dir: yz` at construction
   (@sec-ch04-shallow).
6. *A solver without face pressure is refused on the first $x_1$ sweep* of a compressible deck (the second
   derivation above).

The probe against the pin build confirms items 1 to 4 and 6 (@sec-ch04-framework).

**The excerpt.** The defaults and the factory ({{< code src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp RiemannSolverOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}},
{{< code src/riemann/riemann_solver.cpp RiemannSolverImpl::create >}}) and the row map of every solver body, here
`lmars_impl` ({{< code src/riemann/lmars_impl.h lmars_impl >}}):

```cpp
  op->type() = node["type"].as<std::string>("roe");
  op->dir() = node["dir"].as<std::string>("omni");
  ...
  if (opts->type() == "roe") {
    return p->register_module(name, RoeSolver(opts, p));
  } else if (opts->type() == "lmars") {
  ...
  auto ivx = IPR - dim;
  auto ivy = IVX + ((ivx - IVX) + 1) % 3;
  auto ivz = IVX + ((ivx - IVX) + 2) % 3;
```

The first two lines are item 3; the factory is item 4; the last three lines are @eq-ch04-riemann-frame and the
cyclic tangential rows.

### Limits

1. **Two parser paths.** Deleting the block and deleting only its type are different operations; see the generated defaults above.
2. **`roe` is not projected.** On a gnomonic grid it solves in panel components (@sec-ch04-gnomonic); no test
   runs `roe` on a curved grid.
3. **`upwind` is the scalar solver.** As a hydro solver it is refused wherever $x_1$ is resolved, and elsewhere it
   multiplies by the flux buffer it is handed.
4. **`dir`** matters only to `shallow-roe`; for the other five it is parsed and unused.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-b356ccc3d610]: $p$ — pressure [Pa]

[^rg-a2031683b1d7]: dir — direction selector for solvers that use it
